title: The Pulse Beneath the Job Title: Monthly Readings of Requirements and Tasks from 750 Million Chinese Job Ads
abstract: arXiv:2608.26924v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How do we define an occupation? By its job title? An accountant at a small trading company keeps the books; at a listed firm the same title demands a certified-accountant licence, and the week goes to the reports that regulators and the board read. Same title, different bar, different work. What defines an occupation is who it lets in and what it asks them to do. In a rapidly changing labor market, tracking those requirements and tasks is how to take the market's pulse. Yet no instrument reads both at the speed they change. Official occupational directories like O*NET report one national average per occupation, updated every few years. Job postings are timely but unstructured. Research built on them works from job titles plus proprietary skill keywords, which blur what is asked of a candidate into what a candidate is asked to do. The blur matters, because rising requirements and changing tasks are different events with different causes.

translated_title: 职位头衔之下的脉搏：来自7.5亿中国招聘广告的月度需求与任务分析
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.26924v1 公告类型：新 摘要：我们如何定义一个职业？通过其职位头衔吗？小贸易公司的会计负责记账；而在上市公司，同样的头衔要求持有注册会计师执照，一周的时间都花在监管机构和董事会阅读的报告上。相同的头衔，不同的门槛，不同的工作内容。定义职业的是它允许谁进入以及它要求他们做什么。在快速变化的劳动力市场中，追踪这些要求和任务是把握市场脉搏的方式。然而，没有任何工具能以它们变化的速度同时读取这两者。官方职业目录如O*NET每个职业报告一个全国平均值，每几年更新一次。招聘信息及时但非结构化。基于这些的研究从职位头衔加上专有技能关键词出发，这模糊了候选人的要求与候选人被要求做的工作之间的区别。这种模糊很重要，因为提升的要求和变化的任务是不同原因导致的不同事件。
tldr: 本文通过分析7.5亿中国招聘广告，提出一种方法以月度频率同时追踪职业的要求和任务变化，区分二者以更精确地捕捉劳动力市场动态。
en_tdlr: This paper analyzes 750 million Chinese job ads to propose a method for tracking occupational requirements and tasks at monthly frequency, distinguishing between them to more precisely capture labor market dynamics.
